# Labor poverty (INEGI / CONEVAL ITLP)

I am turning INEGI **Pobreza Laboral (PL)** quarterly estimates (2005-I through 2026-II) into pressures.

A person is in *pobreza laboral* when household labor income is not enough to buy the food basket (*canasta alimentaria*). Higher poverty share = higher pressure (**1 = most pressure**).

**Pros:** quarterly and current through 2025/2026.  
**Cons:** national and **state** level only (no municipality).

We decided that for now, assessing this pressure at the state level is fine, as the resources addressing poverty are likely provided more at the state level anyway.  So, we assess the six GoC states: Baja California, Baja California Sur, Sonora, Sinaloa, Jalisco, and Nayarit.

In this script, I produced **two** pressure scores:

1. **General labor poverty** (Cuadro 9): the % whose labor income cannot buy the food basket.  
2. **LE income pressure** (Cuadro 18): within-industry mean labor income (lower income → higher pressure). This is **not** a poverty rate. Also, we may not include it as a pressure...just exploring what it would look like to include it.

*Outline of the script:*

1. Take a look at what every Cuadro in the workbook contains (and does not).  Each tab is called a Cuadro in the excel sheet available for download here: <https://en.www.inegi.org.mx/desarrollosocial/pl/#tabular_data>
2. Read CONAPO population for year-specific weights of population, which allows us to scale each state by the number of people.
3. Clean Cuadro 9 to obtain a GoC poverty pressure 0-1.  
4. Clean Cuadro 18 to get a within-industry LE income pressure 0-1.  
5. Combine all marine-adjacent industries (there are none that are explicitly marine); apply the population weight across the states.  
6. Explore with `plotly` and save.

```{r setup}
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(knitr)
library(plotly)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  fig.width = 9,
  fig.height = 5,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE
)
```

```{r paths}
pl_path <- here::here("/home/shares/ohi/OHI_GOC/_raw_data/inegi_labor_poverty/pl_2005t_2026t.xlsx") # note that pl = poverty laboral

conapo_path <- here::here("/home/shares/ohi/OHI_GOC/_raw_data/CONAPO_demographic_indicators/d2026/pobproy_ggrupos.csv")

output_dir <- "/home/shares/ohi/OHI_GOC/goal_prep/pressures/labor_poverty/output"
dir.create(output_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
```

```{r peek-contenido}
contenido <- read_excel(
  pl_path,
  sheet = "Contenido",
  col_names = FALSE,
  .name_repair = "minimal"
) |> 
  janitor::clean_names() |> 
  dplyr::select(x, x_3)

# first two columns are the sheet name and its description
colnames(contenido)[1:2] <- c("sheet", "description")

contenido_tidy <- contenido %>%
  select(1:2) %>%
  setNames(c("sheet", "description")) %>%
  mutate(

  kable(caption = "INEGI pobreza laboral workbook - contenido")
```

### What I understand each Cuadro to be

After going through it, here is what I think each tab has, and what it does **not** provide us:

| Sheet | What it does have | What it does **not** have |
|---|---|---|
| **Cuadro 1** | ITLP (índice de la tendencia laboral de la pobreza), national + rural/urban | state or industry information |
| **Cuadro 2** | % of people in labor poverty, national + rural/urban | state or industry information |
| **Cuadro 3** | labor income per capita, national + rural/urban | poverty rate; state/industry |
| **Cuadro 4** | wage mass (*masa salarial*), national + rural/urban | poverty rate; state/industry |
| **Cuadro 5** | labor income per capita **by state** | poverty rate; industry |
| **Cuadro 6** | labor poverty indicators by sex of household head | national only, so missing information at a higher resolution |
| **Cuadro 7** | wage mass **by state** | poverty rate; industry |
| **Cuadro 8** | ITLP **by state** | industry; not the % poverty rate itself |
| **Cuadro 9** | **% in labor poverty by state**: my main poverty pressure | municipality; industry |
| **Cuadro 10** | % in labor poverty for self-represented cities | full GoC coastal coverage, has only 3 cities across the GoC (not including Mexicali) |
| **Cuadro 11** | labor-force participation by age × rural/urban | poverty rate by state |
| **Cuadro 12** | school attendance ages 5-17 × rural/urban | poverty / income |
| **Cuadro 13** | occupied population in labor poverty by sex | state × industry |
| **Cuadro 14** | occupied population in labor poverty, indigenous municipality flag | GoC states I need |
| **Cuadro 15** | occupied population in labor poverty by age | state × industry |
| **Cuadro 16** | occupied population in labor poverty by formality | state × industry |
| **Cuadro 17** | mean labor income by sex × state | poverty rate; industry |
| **Cuadro 18.*** | mean labor income of the occupied population **by industry**, one sheet per state (and EUM) | poverty %; municipality; specific marine sectors |

So for this script I only clean **Cuadro 9** (pressure 1) and **Cuadro 18** for the six GoC states (pressure 2). Everything else I leave alone for now.

Note that Cuadro 18 is **average labor income in constant pesos** (base = first quarter of 2020), not a poverty percentage. `NA` cells appear when ENOE cannot support an estimate for that state/industry/quarter.

## 2. CONAPO state population (year-specific weights)

`pobproy_ggrupos.csv` is municipality × sex × year. Here, I sum `POB_TOTAL` so each GoC state-year has one population weight. It is not often we are wanting the state population haha!!

```{r conapo-read}
conapo_raw <- read_csv(conapo_path)
```

```{r conapo-aggregate}
state_population <- conapo_raw %>%
  select(CLAVE_ENT, NOM_ENT, ANO, SEXO, POB_TOTAL) %>%
  filter(NOM_ENT %in% goc_states) %>%
  group_by(year = ANO, estado = NOM_ENT) %>%
  # sum men + women across all municipalities in the state
  summarize(poblacion = sum(POB_TOTAL, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r conapo-check}
state_population %>%
  filter(year %in% c(2005, 2010, 2020, 2025)) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = poblacion) %>%
  kable(
    caption = "CONAPO projected total population (GoC states; selected years)",
    format.args = list(big.mark = ",")
  )

stopifnot(all(goc_states %in% unique(state_population$estado)))
```

## 3. Clean Cuadro 9: labor poverty % by state

Year is only printed on the first quarter of each year, so I fill it down. Quarter labels sometimes carry footnotes (e.g. `IV3/`), so I remove those. 

```{r cuadro9-header}
# pull header cells as a plain character vector (avoids empty colnames)
c9_header <- read_excel(
  pl_path,
  sheet = "Cuadro 9",
  range = cell_rows(6),
  col_names = FALSE,
  .name_repair = "unique"
) %>%
  unlist(use.names = FALSE) %>%
  as.character() %>%
  str_trim()
```

```{r cuadro9-data}
# skip the title block; data start at excel row 7
c9_data <- read_excel(
  pl_path,
  sheet = "Cuadro 9",
  skip = 6,
  col_names = FALSE,
  col_types = "text",
  .name_repair = "unique"
)

# replace placeholder colnames with the real excel header row
colnames(c9_data) <- make.unique(c9_header)
colnames(c9_data)[1:2] <- c("year", "quarter")
```

```{r cuadro9-tidy-year-quarter}
# clean it for all of the states before selecting for GoC!!
c9_tidy <- c9_data %>%
  mutate(
    # pull the year (later quarters leave this blank)
    year = as.integer(str_extract(year, "^[0-9]{4}")),
    # keep only roman numerals (drop footnote junk like 3/)
    quarter = str_trim(str_replace_all(as.character(quarter), "[^IVX]", "")),
    quarter = factor(quarter, levels = c("I", "II", "III", "IV"), ordered = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  # carry the printed year down through ii, iii, iv
  fill(year, .direction = "down") %>%
  filter(!is.na(year), !is.na(quarter), quarter %in% c("I", "II", "III", "IV"))
```

```{r cuadro9-long-goc}
pl_state_long <- c9_tidy %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(year, quarter),
    names_to = "estado",
    values_to = "poverty_pct_raw"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    estado = str_trim(estado),
    # non-numeric cells (na, nd, notes) become na
    poverty_pct = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(poverty_pct_raw))
  ) %>%
  filter(estado %in% goc_states) %>%
  select(year, quarter, estado, poverty_pct) %>%
  mutate(
    year_q = paste0(year, "-", as.character(quarter)),
    # decimal year for plotting (i=0, ii=0.25, iii=0.5, iv=0.75)
    time = year + (as.integer(quarter) - 1) / 4 
  ) %>%
  arrange(estado, year, quarter)
```

```{r cuadro9-summary}
pl_state_long %>%
  count(estado, name = "n_quarters") %>%
  kable(caption = "GoC states: quarters with Cuadro 9 rows (includes NA poverty cells)")

pl_state_long %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    n_missing = sum(is.na(poverty_pct)),
    min_pct = min(poverty_pct, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_pct = max(poverty_pct, na.rm = TRUE),
    years = paste(range(year, na.rm = TRUE), collapse = "-")
  ) %>%
  kable(digits = 2, caption = "Cuadro 9 GoC summary")

# |   n| n_missing| min_pct| max_pct|years     |
# |---:|---------:|-------:|-------:|:---------|
# | 516|         6|   10.75|   41.27|2005-2026 |
```

I expect **2020-II** to be missing nationally because ENOE collection was suspended during COVID.

```{r cuadro9-missing}
pl_state_long %>%
  filter(is.na(poverty_pct)) %>%
  count(year, quarter, name = "n_states_missing") %>%
  kable(caption = "Missing poverty cells in GoC Cuadro 9 extract")

# YUP!
# | year|quarter | n_states_missing|
# |----:|:-------|----------------:|
# | 2020|II      |                6|
```

## 4. Rescale Cuadro 9 → general poverty pressure 0-1

Here I bring together **all GoC state-quarters** and set the 90th percentile to pressure = 1. Higher `poverty_pct` = a higher pressure.

Before locking that in, I also compute two alternatives and compare **2025** scores:

| Option | Formula | What pressure = 1 means |
|---|---|---|
| **A. GoC 90th** | `(pct - GoC min) / (GoC p90 - GoC min)`, clipped | among the worst GoC state-quarters |
| **B. Absolute /100** | `pct / 100` | everyone in labor poverty |
| **C. Mexico 90th** | `(pct - MX min) / (MX p90 - MX min)`, clipped | as bad as the national high end |

```{r poverty-refs}
pl_obs <- pl_state_long %>% filter(!is.na(poverty_pct))

ref_low <- min(pl_obs$poverty_pct)

# 90th percentile of the pooled goC series becomes pressure = 1
ref_high <- as.numeric(quantile(pl_obs$poverty_pct, probs = quantile_p))

stopifnot(is.finite(ref_low), is.finite(ref_high), ref_high > ref_low)
```

```{r poverty-scale}
pl_scaled <- pl_state_long %>%
  mutate(
    pressure = (poverty_pct - ref_low) / (ref_high - ref_low),
    # clip anything outside 0-1 (values above the 90th pct become 1)
    pressure = pmin(pmax(pressure, 0), 1)
  )
```

```{r poverty-scale-table}
tibble(
  quantile = quantile_p,
  poverty_min = ref_low,
  poverty_max = ref_high,
  n_state_quarters = nrow(pl_obs),
  n_at_one = sum(pl_scaled$pressure == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
) %>%
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "Rescaled GoC labor poverty (Cuadro 9) - option A")

# | quantile| poverty_min| poverty_max| n_state_quarters| n_at_one|
# |--------:|-----------:|-----------:|----------------:|--------:|
# |      0.9|      10.748|      33.612|              510|       51|
```

### Optional annual mean (option A)

If I later want one value per year, I average the available quarters (unweighted).

```{r poverty-annual}
pl_annual <- pl_scaled %>%
  filter(!is.na(pressure)) %>%
  group_by(year, estado) %>%
  summarise(
    n_quarters = n(),
    poverty_pct = mean(poverty_pct),
    pressure = mean(pressure),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r poverty-annual-table}
pl_annual %>%
  filter(year == max(year)) %>%
  arrange(desc(pressure)) %>%
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "Latest available year: annual mean pressure by state (option A)")

# | year|estado              | n_quarters| poverty_pct| pressure|
# |----:|:-------------------|----------:|-----------:|--------:|
# | 2026|Sinaloa             |          2|      26.985|    0.710|
# | 2026|Sonora              |          2|      23.478|    0.557|
# | 2026|Jalisco             |          2|      23.362|    0.552|
# | 2026|Nayarit             |          2|      23.260|    0.547|
# | 2026|Baja California     |          2|      16.824|    0.266|
# | 2026|Baja California Sur |          2|      13.988|    0.142|
```

### Compare three rescales (focus on 2025)

```{r poverty-mexico-long}
# all mexico states for option C (drop the national aggregate column)
pl_mexico_long <- c9_tidy %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c(year, quarter),
    names_to = "estado",
    values_to = "poverty_pct_raw"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    estado = str_trim(estado),
    poverty_pct = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(poverty_pct_raw))
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(poverty_pct),
    !str_detect(estado, regex("Estados Unidos Mexicanos", ignore_case = TRUE))
  ) %>%
  select(year, quarter, estado, poverty_pct)
```

```{r poverty-refs-three}
# option a refs (same as above)
ref_goc_low  <- ref_low
ref_goc_high <- ref_high

# option c refs: all mexico state-quarters
ref_mx_low  <- min(pl_mexico_long$poverty_pct)
ref_mx_high <- as.numeric(quantile(pl_mexico_long$poverty_pct, probs = quantile_p))

stopifnot(ref_mx_high > ref_mx_low)

tibble(
  option = c("A. GoC 90th", "B. Absolute 100% in labor poverty", "C. Mexico 90th"),
  ref_low = c(ref_goc_low, 0, ref_mx_low),
  ref_high = c(ref_goc_high, 100, ref_mx_high),
  n_obs_in_ref = c(nrow(pl_obs), NA_integer_, nrow(pl_mexico_long))
) %>%
  kable(digits = 2, caption = "Reference anchors for the three Cuadro 9 rescales")

# |option           | ref_low| ref_high| n_obs_in_ref|
# |:----------------|-------:|--------:|------------:|
# |A. GoC 90th      |   10.75|    33.61|          510|
# |B. Absolute 100% in labor poverty |    0.00|   100.00|           NA|
# |C. Mexico 90th   |   10.75|    55.96|         2719|
```

```{r poverty-scale-three}
pl_scaled_compare <- pl_state_long %>%
  mutate(
    # a: relative to goC history
    pressure_goc90 = (poverty_pct - ref_goc_low) / (ref_goc_high - ref_goc_low),
    pressure_goc90 = pmin(pmax(pressure_goc90, 0), 1),
    # b: absolute share in poverty
    pressure_pct100 = poverty_pct / 100,
    pressure_pct100 = pmin(pmax(pressure_pct100, 0), 1),
    # c: relative to all mexico states
    pressure_mx90 = (poverty_pct - ref_mx_low) / (ref_mx_high - ref_mx_low),
    pressure_mx90 = pmin(pmax(pressure_mx90, 0), 1)
  )
```

```{r poverty-compare-2025}
# annual mean for 2025 under each option
pl_compare_2025 <- pl_scaled_compare %>%
  filter(year == 2025, !is.na(poverty_pct)) %>%
  group_by(estado) %>%
  summarise(
    n_quarters = n(),
    poverty_pct = mean(poverty_pct),
    pressure_goc90 = mean(pressure_goc90),
    pressure_pct100 = mean(pressure_pct100),
    pressure_mx90 = mean(pressure_mx90),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(poverty_pct))

pl_compare_2025 %>%
  kable(
    digits = 3,
    caption = "2025 GoC labor poverty: raw % and pressure under three rescales"
  )

# |estado              | n_quarters| poverty_pct| pressure_goc90| pressure_pct100| pressure_mx90|
# |:-------------------|----------:|-----------:|--------------:|---------------:|-------------:|
# |Sonora              |          4|      26.575|          0.692|           0.266|         0.350|
# |Sinaloa             |          4|      25.477|          0.644|           0.255|         0.326|
# |Nayarit             |          4|      24.171|          0.587|           0.242|         0.297|
# |Jalisco             |          4|      23.338|          0.551|           0.233|         0.278|
# |Baja California     |          4|      19.395|          0.378|           0.194|         0.191|
# |Baja California Sur |          4|      13.358|          0.114|           0.134|         0.058|
```

```{r poverty-compare-2025-long}
pl_compare_2025_long <- pl_compare_2025 %>%
  select(estado, poverty_pct, pressure_goc90, pressure_pct100, pressure_mx90) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("pressure_"),
    names_to = "rescale",
    values_to = "pressure"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    rescale = recode(
      rescale,
      pressure_goc90 = "A. GoC 90th",
      pressure_pct100 = "B. Absolute 100% in labor poverty",
      pressure_mx90 = "C. Mexico 90th"
    )
  )
```

```{r poverty-compare-timeseries}
# goC mean across states over time under each option
pl_compare_ts <- pl_scaled_compare %>%
  filter(!is.na(poverty_pct)) %>%
  group_by(year, quarter, time) %>%
  summarise(
    pressure_goc90 = mean(pressure_goc90),
    pressure_pct100 = mean(pressure_pct100),
    pressure_mx90 = mean(pressure_mx90),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("pressure_"),
    names_to = "rescale",
    values_to = "pressure"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    rescale = recode(
      rescale,
      pressure_goc90 = "A. GoC 90th",
      pressure_pct100 = "B. Absolute 100% in labor poverty",
      pressure_mx90 = "C. Mexico 90th"
    )
  )

plot_compare_ts <- plot_ly(
  pl_compare_ts,
  x = ~time,
  y = ~pressure,
  color = ~rescale,
  type = "scatter",
  mode = "lines"
) %>%
  layout(
    title = "GoC mean poverty pressure over time: three options for rescaling",
    xaxis = list(title = "Year"),
    yaxis = list(title = "Mean pressure (0-1)", range = c(0, 1.05))
  )

plot_compare_ts
```


I am keeping **Option B** for now (`pressure = poverty_pct / 100`). It is easy to swap to A or C later by changing which column becomes `pl_scaled` below.

```{r save-option-b}
# Option B: absolute share in labor poverty (1 = 100% of people in poverty)
pl_scaled <- pl_scaled_compare %>%
  transmute(
    year, quarter, time, year_q, estado,
    poverty_pct,
    pressure = pressure_pct100
  )

pl_annual <- pl_scaled %>%
  filter(!is.na(pressure)) %>%
  group_by(year, estado) %>%
  summarise(
    n_quarters = n(),
    poverty_pct = mean(poverty_pct),
    pressure = mean(pressure),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

pl_annual %>%
  filter(year == 2025) %>%
  arrange(desc(pressure)) %>%
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "Using Option B: 2025 annual mean pressure by state")

# | year|estado              | n_quarters| poverty_pct| pressure|
# |----:|:-------------------|----------:|-----------:|--------:|
# | 2025|Sonora              |          4|      26.575|    0.266|
# | 2025|Sinaloa             |          4|      25.477|    0.255|
# | 2025|Nayarit             |          4|      24.171|    0.242|
# | 2025|Jalisco             |          4|      23.338|    0.233|
# | 2025|Baja California     |          4|      19.395|    0.194|
# | 2025|Baja California Sur |          4|      13.358|    0.134|
```


## 5. Choosing Option B and saving it (`rgn_id`, `year`, `pressure`)

State Cuadro 9 values are inherited by every GoC `rgn_id` that sits in that state (`municipality_to_rgnid_update.csv`). Region_9 spans Jalisco and Nayarit, so for that region I take a CONAPO population-weighted mean of the two state pressures.

```{r mun-rgn-lookup}
mun_lookup <- read_csv(here::here("/home/shares/ohi/OHI_GOC/spatial/municipality_to_rgnid/municipality_to_rgnid_update.csv")) %>%
  mutate(
    estado = str_trim(estado),
    rgn_id = as.character(rgn_id)
  )

estado_to_rgn <- mun_lookup %>%
  distinct(estado, rgn_id) %>%
  mutate(estado_key = str_to_upper(estado)) %>%
  select(estado_key, rgn_id)

estado_to_rgn %>%
  arrange(rgn_id, estado_key) %>%
  kable(caption = "Estado → rgn_id (unique pairs from municipality lookup)")

# |estado_key          |rgn_id   |
# |:-------------------|:--------|
# |BAJA CALIFORNIA     |Region_1 |
# |BAJA CALIFORNIA     |Region_2 |
# |BAJA CALIFORNIA SUR |Region_3 |
# |BAJA CALIFORNIA SUR |Region_4 |
# |SONORA              |Region_5 |
# |SONORA              |Region_6 |
# |SONORA              |Region_7 |
# |SINALOA             |Region_8 |
# |JALISCO             |Region_9 |
# |NAYARIT             |Region_9 |
```

```{r option-b-to-rgn}
pl_rgn_annual <- pl_annual %>%
  mutate(estado_key = str_to_upper(estado)) %>%
  left_join(estado_to_rgn, by = "estado_key", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
  left_join(state_population, by = c("year", "estado")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(rgn_id), !is.na(pressure))

# one row per rgn_id × year; pop-weight when a region spans 2+ states (Region_9)
poverty_laboral_pressure <- pl_rgn_annual %>%
  group_by(rgn_id, year) %>%
  summarise(
    pressure = if (n() == 1 || all(is.na(poblacion))) {
      mean(pressure)
    } else {
      weighted.mean(pressure, w = poblacion, na.rm = TRUE)
    },
    n_states = n_distinct(estado),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    rgn_num = as.integer(str_remove(rgn_id, "Region_")),
    pressure = round(pressure, 4)
  ) %>%
  arrange(year, rgn_num) %>%
  select(rgn_id, year, pressure)

poverty_laboral_pressure %>%
  filter(year == 2025) %>%
  kable(digits = 4, caption = "Option B labor poverty pressure by rgn_id (2025)")

# |rgn_id   | year| pressure|
# |:--------|----:|--------:|
# |Region_1 | 2025|   0.1940|
# |Region_2 | 2025|   0.1940|
# |Region_3 | 2025|   0.1336|
# |Region_4 | 2025|   0.1336|
# |Region_5 | 2025|   0.2658|
# |Region_6 | 2025|   0.2658|
# |Region_7 | 2025|   0.2658|
# |Region_8 | 2025|   0.2548|
# |Region_9 | 2025|   0.2345|
```

```{r save-option-b}
mazu_csv <- write_csv(poverty_laboral_pressure, here::here(output_dir, "poverty_laboral_pressure.csv"))
github_csv <- write_csv(poverty_laboral_pressure, here::here("_pressures/social/output", "poverty_laboral_pressure.csv"))
```


## 6. LE POTENTIAL PRESSURE: Clean Cuadro 18: mean labor income by industry × state

I read each GoC state's Cuadro 18 sheet the same way, then bind them.

```{r cuadro18-sheet-map}
# sheet name in the workbook and the estado label I want in the tidy data
goc_cuadro18_sheets <- tribble(
  ~sheet, ~estado,
  "Cuadro 18.BC", "Baja California",
  "Cuadro 18.BCS", "Baja California Sur",
  "Cuadro 18.Son.", "Sonora",
  "Cuadro 18.Sin.", "Sinaloa",
  "Cuadro 18.Jal.", "Jalisco",
  "Cuadro 18.Nay.", "Nayarit"
)
```


```{r cuadro18-read-loop}
pl_industry_list <- list()

for (i in seq_len(nrow(goc_cuadro18_sheets))) {
  sheet_i <- goc_cuadro18_sheets$sheet[i]
  estado_i <- goc_cuadro18_sheets$estado[i]

  # industry names live on excel row 7; unlist so colnames stay usable
  header_i <- read_excel(
    pl_path,
    sheet = sheet_i,
    range = cell_rows(7),
    col_names = FALSE,
    .name_repair = "unique"
  ) %>%
    unlist(use.names = FALSE) %>%
    as.character() %>%
    str_trim()

  dat_i <- read_excel(
    pl_path,
    sheet = sheet_i,
    skip = 7,
    col_names = FALSE,
    col_types = "text",
    .name_repair = "unique"
  )

  colnames(dat_i) <- make.unique(header_i)
  colnames(dat_i)[1:2] <- c("year", "quarter")

  dat_i <- dat_i %>%
    mutate(
      year = as.integer(str_extract(year, "^[0-9]{4}")),
      quarter = str_trim(str_replace_all(as.character(quarter), "[^IVX]", "")),
      quarter = factor(quarter, levels = c("I", "II", "III", "IV"), ordered = TRUE),
      estado = estado_i
    ) %>%
    fill(year, .direction = "down") %>%
    filter(!is.na(year), quarter %in% c("I", "II", "III", "IV")) %>%
    pivot_longer(
      cols = -c(year, quarter, estado),
      names_to = "industry_raw",
      values_to = "income_raw"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      industry_raw = str_trim(industry_raw),
      income = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(income_raw))
    ) %>%
    select(year, quarter, estado, industry_raw, income)

  pl_industry_list[[i]] <- dat_i
}
```

```{r cuadro18-bind}
pl_industry_long <- bind_rows(pl_industry_list) %>%
  left_join(industry_lookup, by = "industry_raw") %>%
  mutate(
    year_q = paste0(year, "-", as.character(quarter)),
    time = year + (as.integer(quarter) - 1) / 4,
    marine_adjacent = industry %in% marine_adjacent_industries
  )
```

```{r cuadro18-check-mapping}
# every raw industry name from inegi should match my lookup table
unmapped <- pl_industry_long %>%
  filter(is.na(industry)) %>%
  distinct(industry_raw)

stopifnot(nrow(unmapped) == 0)

pl_industry_long %>%
  count(industry, marine_adjacent) %>%
  kable(caption = "Cuadro 18 industries (GoC states)")
```

## 7. Rescale Cuadro 18 → LE income pressure 0-1

Low income → high pressure. High income → low pressure.

Incomes are **right-skewed**: a few `income_max` values sit well above `income_p90`. I do **not** want those rich outliers to set pressure = 0.

I **do** want extreme poor to still reach pressure = 1.

**Asymmetric scale (within each industry):**

| Anchor | Role |
|---|---|
| `income_min` | pressure = **1** (extreme poor still count) |
| `income_p90` | pressure = **0** (rich tail trimmed) |
| above p90 | clipped to 0 |

```{r le-rescale}
income_p_high <- 0.90

pl_industry_scaled <- pl_industry_long %>%
  group_by(industry) %>%
  mutate(
    # poorest observed income in this industry across goC state-quarters
    income_min_ind = min(income, na.rm = TRUE),
    # trim the rich end so a few high outliers do not stretch the scale
    income_p90_ind = as.numeric(quantile(income, probs = income_p_high, na.rm = TRUE)),
    # map [min, p90] → [1, 0]
    pressure_income = (income_p90_ind - income) / (income_p90_ind - income_min_ind),
    pressure_income = pmin(pmax(pressure_income, 0), 1)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(-income_min_ind, -income_p90_ind)
```

```{r le-join-population}
# year-specific conapo weight for each state-quarter
pl_industry_scaled <- pl_industry_scaled %>%
  left_join(state_population, by = c("year", "estado"))

n_missing_pop <- sum(is.na(pl_industry_scaled$poblacion))
if (n_missing_pop > 0) {
  warning(n_missing_pop, " industry rows missing CONAPO population join")
}
```

```{r le-summary-table}
pl_industry_scaled %>%
  filter(!is.na(income), !is.na(poblacion)) %>%
  group_by(industry, marine_adjacent) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    income_min = min(income),
    income_p50 = as.numeric(quantile(income, 0.5)),
    income_p90 = as.numeric(quantile(income, income_p_high)),
    income_max = max(income),
    pressure_mean_unweighted = mean(pressure_income),
    # larger states pull the mean more
    pressure_mean_popwt = weighted.mean(pressure_income, w = poblacion),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(marine_adjacent), industry) %>%
  kable(
    digits = 1,
    caption = "Within-industry LE pressure (min→1, p90→0); unweighted vs CONAPO pop-weighted mean"
  )
```

## 8. Combine marine-adjacent industries

For each state-quarter I average the three marine-adjacent industry pressures (equal industry weights for now). Then I roll up across states with that year's CONAPO population.

```{r le-by-state-quarter}
pl_le_marine <- pl_industry_scaled %>%
  filter(marine_adjacent, !is.na(pressure_income), !is.na(poblacion)) %>%
  group_by(year, quarter, year_q, time, estado, poblacion) %>%
  summarise(
    n_industries = n(),
    pressure_le = mean(pressure_income),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r le-gulf}
pl_le_gulf <- pl_le_marine %>%
  group_by(year, quarter, year_q, time) %>%
  summarise(
    pressure_le_popwt = weighted.mean(pressure_le, w = poblacion),
    pressure_le_unwt = mean(pressure_le),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r le-state-table}
pl_le_marine %>%
  group_by(estado) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_pressure_le = mean(pressure_le),
    # show one year of population for context
    poblacion_2020 = poblacion[year == 2020][1],
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_pressure_le)) %>%
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "Mean LE marine-adjacent pressure by state (CONAPO 2020 pop shown)")
```

```{r le-industry-by-state-table}
pl_industry_scaled %>%
  filter(marine_adjacent, !is.na(pressure_income)) %>%
  group_by(estado, industry) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_pressure = mean(pressure_income),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = industry, values_from = mean_pressure) %>%
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "Mean income-pressure by state × marine-adjacent industry")
```

```{r plot-poverty}
plot_poverty <- plot_ly(

  x = ~time,
  y = ~pressure,
  color = ~estado,
  type = "scatter",
  mode = "lines",
  text = ~paste0(

) %>%

    title = "Labor poverty pressure (Cuadro 9, Option B Absolute 100% labor poverty ref)",

  )

plot_poverty
```

### LE income pressure by marine-adjacent industries

```{r plot-industry}
plot_industry <- plot_ly(
  pl_industry_scaled %>% filter(marine_adjacent, !is.na(pressure_income)),
  x = ~time,
  y = ~pressure_income,
  color = ~estado,
  linetype = ~industry,
  type = "scatter",
  mode = "lines",
  text = ~paste0(
    estado, " | ", industry, "<br>", year_q,

  )

plot_industry
```

### Combined LE marine pressure: Gulf pop-weighted vs unweighted

```{r plot-le-gulf}
plot_le_gulf <- plot_ly(pl_le_gulf, x = ~time) %>%
  add_lines(
    y = ~pressure_le_popwt,
    name = "population-weighted",
    text = ~paste0(year_q, "<br>pop-wt: ", round(pressure_le_popwt, 3)),
    hoverinfo = "text"
  ) %>%
  add_lines(
    y = ~pressure_le_unwt,
    name = "unweighted (states equal)",
    text = ~paste0(year_q, "<br>unwt: ", round(pressure_le_unwt, 3)),
    hoverinfo = "text"
  ) %>%
  layout(
    title = "Combined LE marine-adjacent pressure - GoC",
    xaxis = list(title = "Year"),
    yaxis = list(title = "Pressure (0-1)", range = c(0, 1.05))
  )

plot_le_gulf
```
